finite-cover-certificate.title: Finite interval-cover certificate for the interrupted Pell covering job
finite-cover-certificate.hypothesis: ThirtyCofactorPellCovering is a finite covering statement, not a Pell-solvability theorem. A certificate that separates the four possible M values, exact integer bounds for L, and the resulting 25 (M,L) pairs should let Lean check the job compositionally. This should reduce repair loops because each obligation is a small arithmetic fact and the frozen theorem type is never weakened.
procedure: Reopen ThirtyCofactorPellCovering-2987558f and record the four frozen goals and exact types; do not edit theorem statements.
Prove cofactor_M_cases from gcd divisibility: gcd n 3 divides 3 and gcd(n-1) 6 divides 6, and the two factors cannot both contribute a factor 3, so the product lies in {1,2,3,6}.
Normalize M*r^2 = L*n*(n-1). From 3n<r derive L>9M, hence 9M+1<=L. From 3r<10n and n>=104 derive 927L<10400M by cross-multiplication.
Split on M in {1,2,3,6}; convert each strict rational interval into explicit integer lower and upper bounds for L.
Define the explicit 25-pair list (1,10..11), (2,19..22), (3,28..33), (6,55..67) and prove the disjunction for L by interval arithmetic.
Package the four goals into the fixed module; compile with real Lean and inspect exact errors before any repair.
If nonlinear gcd normalization blocks, add small helper lemmas for gcd divisibility and integer division rather than changing hypotheses.
finite-cover-certificate.success_criterion: All four frozen goals of ThirtyCofactorPellCovering-2987558f compile with Lean exit 0, only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound, no holes or native_decide, and unchanged theorem types; the job is accepted and publishable.
finite-cover-certificate.failure_criterion: If the derived interval admits an L outside the 25 pairs, or Lean cannot close a specific gcd/division obligation after exact diagnosis, record the failing goal and interval; revise the certificate or drop the method. An interrupted or usage-missing run is not counted as mathematical failure.
finite-cover-certificate.author: DeepSeek

defect-localization.title: Localize the remaining obstruction in the exact square defect before global Pell search
defect-localization.hypothesis: The v16 exact denominator delta=Q/gcd(Q,r^2) and primitive defect H impose p-adic constraints stronger than the global Pell equation alone. Proving these local constraints as reusable Lean lemmas can eliminate entire delta-families or reduce the final ThirtyCofactorGoal to finite congruence/valuation obligations, without assuming Pell completeness, Bennett, or a new Thue theorem.
procedure: Formalize the v16 identities delta | r, delta^3 | Q, and gcd(delta,H)=1 with exact hypotheses as small Lean lemmas.
For each prime p | delta, derive v_p(A)=v_p(Q) and the allowed range of v_p(r) from Q | r^3; separate p=2,3 and p>=5.
Combine these valuations with 3n<r<10n/3, S | (n-2), and the cofactor condition to obtain congruence restrictions on n modulo p^e.
Use the restrictions to rule out a nontrivial delta-family or to produce a finite residue table; do not introduce an unproved distribution or Pell-completeness assumption.
Feed only the resulting fixed lemmas to the goal worker and compare against the frozen baseline; record whether the final target's hypothesis set actually shrinks.
defect-localization.success_criterion: At least one new fixed Lean lemma eliminates a nontrivial delta-family or strictly reduces the hypotheses needed by a frozen target, with no new assumptions and real Lean verification.
defect-localization.failure_criterion: If the local valuations are compatible with all delta>=13, or the reduction needs an unproved prime-distribution/Thue/Pell theorem, record the compatible family or missing lemma and revise or drop the method. A written v16 argument or Python audit is not counted as Lean success.
defect-localization.author: DeepSeek

evaluations.model_conclusion: Accepted trial: all four frozen obligations (exponent_domain_iff, q_bound_ge_five, q_bound_two, q_bound_three) pass real Lean with only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound and no hand edits. Measured: 5 attempt records, 55030 reported completion tokens (53719 reasoning), 14.339s recorded Lean time over 5 timed attempts, error classes {unused_binding:5, proof_gap:1}, zero seed recompilations, zero attempts without usage. The predicted split held in the weak sense only: the three polynomial bounds closed quickly as small monotone-power comparisons, but the substantive obligation was not an interval cover at all — exponent_domain_iff is a pure omega-arithmetic equivalence, and the q_bounds are power-monotonicity chains. Across four trials on this method (PellCovering, Valuation, PellReduction, ExponentDomain) the recurring transferable element is 'split the frozen statement into small independent integer obligations with explicit bounds and prove each separately', while the interval-cover/certificate-list part was actually used only in the PellCovering trial. Limitations: sequential non-randomized trials, empty matched baselines, candidate-response token scope excludes planner/scope/repair critics, and this module proves only the exponent-domain equivalence and three polynomial bounds — not p ≤ 6w, not n < 9w^4+2, not Q∤r², and neither frozen target.
